cards.originalFull: This chapter addresses Scenario~S1, the most controlled setting in the thesis map. Here the symbolic notes and their timing are already known, but the note-level velocity is missing, flattened, or musically uninformative. The chapter therefore asks a focused question: can useful note-level dynamics be recovered from symbolic structure alone, without changing the original composition?

cards.reviewStatus: 旧轮已复核，待作者选择
cards.reviewerComment: Section 3.1: This work is mentioned as the “most controlled” in the thesis; however predicting dynamics from a score in the absence of any dynamics markings or velocity info is a more unconstrained problem than dynamics prediction given input audio (where dynamics are present).
cards.authorResponse: > Yes my mistake, my intend is to say "less input signal compared to others", but indeed less constrained. I will change my term.
cards.contextAfter: This setting matters because it isolates the dynamics problem from the broader transcription problem. It is common in digital audio workstation workflows, step-entered MIDI, quantised MIDI, and corpus curation settings where note content already exists but expression does not. It also provides the cleanest test of the thesis claim that dynamics can be treated as a separate and editable target rather than as a side effect of full expressive performance generation.

cards.originalFocus: This hybrid supervision is useful because it constrains both the local onset value and the broader note sustain region, while still keeping note-level precision central to the objective.

options.label: A · 最短解释
options.focusText: Each component is averaged over its own mask, and the two means have equal relative coefficients. Equal coefficients do not imply equal numerical loss or gradient magnitudes.

options.label: B · 保留 SMC 初步比较
options.focusText: The frame-wise BCE and onset-wise L1 terms are averaged over their respective active positions and combined with equal relative coefficients. We retain the hybrid objective of Kim et al. (2024), supported by the preliminary comparison with frame-only and onset-only supervision reported in our associated SMC paper. Equal coefficients do not imply equal numerical loss or gradient magnitudes.

options.label: C · 解释两项作用
options.focusText: The two terms supervise complementary parts of the note representation: frame-wise BCE covers the active note region, while onset-wise L1 directly penalises the velocity read during post-processing. Each term is averaged over its own active positions, and the two means receive equal relative coefficients. This retains the hybrid formulation used in the prior work and our preliminary verification.

cards.originalFull: This chapter has verified that note-level dynamics can be recovered usefully even when the symbolic notes and timing are held fixed. It turns expressive enhancement into a controllable post-processing stage rather than a full performance-rendering problem, which is exactly the setting encountered in many MIDI-production and corpus-curation workflows.

cards.originalFull:
\paragraph{Results.}
Although a substantial gap to human performance remains, the proposed U-Net clearly outperforms the other systems.
The Flat model performs worst, consistent with earlier findings that default velocity is musically inadequate \cite{kuo2021velocity}.
The seen, less-seen, and unseen repertoire groups are best interpreted as descriptive groups rather than as a strict complexity-controlled comparison.
Even so, the relatively narrow 95\% confidence intervals across groups suggest that participants rated the stimuli with reasonable consistency.

cards.reviewerComment: The perceptual evaluation in Chapter 3 is useful but modest in scale, with 11 expert listeners. This does not invalidate the work, but the thesis should more clearly and explicitly state that the listening test supports the objective results rather than providing deﬁnitive perceptual validation.
